I fixed the handshake failure by making the debug build trust the dev server's self-signed CA. I could not build or run the app here, so this is verified by reading the config only.

**Cause:** The debug build calls `https://10.0.2.2:8443/`, which is signed by the dev CA in `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`. The emulator doesn't trust that CA, so the TLS handshake fails. `CatalogClient` uses a default `OkHttpClient`, which only trusts the system store.

**Changes (all new files, under `app/src/debug/` so release is untouched):**
- `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem`: a copy of the dev CA certificate.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`: a `domain-config` that trusts that certificate only for host `10.0.2.2`.
- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`: a debug manifest overlay that sets `android:networkSecurityConfig` on the application. It merges only into debug builds.

**Choices I made:**
- I scoped trust to `10.0.2.2` rather than trusting the CA for all hosts, so the debug build can't accept this CA anywhere else.
- I copied the PEM into the app instead of referencing `dev-ca/`, because Android resources can only come from inside the module.

**Caveat:** If the dev server's certificate is regenerated, the copy in `app/src/debug/res/raw/` must be updated too. Otherwise the same error will come back.
